Dependencies aren't installed, so a typecheck isn't possible locally; the change is plain TS. Running the check:
The remaining one is deck, assigned inside a callback so narrowing is lost. I'll find it with a helper that returns the value.
Search order is unchanged (pre-order, first match wins). Re-checking:

The null-dereference in buildTemplate is fixed, and Predictable Code's check now says gone. Total findings dropped from 27 to 23, with nothing new reported. I couldn't run the TypeScript compiler or the tests because the project's dependencies aren't installed here.

There were two places in scripts/build-mcp-metadata.ts where a value might be missing:

1. Sample asset paths (the reported line 576): the code used assets.get(a)!, which assumes every lookup finds something. It now builds the asset map with a loop and skips any name that has no path. This can't drop anything in practice, because a name only gets into sampleAssets if it's already in assets.
2. deck: after the first fix, the check flagged this one instead. It was set inside a callback, so the earlier if (!deck) check didn't carry through to where it was used. I added a small findDeck(node) helper that returns the first <Deck> element, or undefined if there is none. It searches in the same order as before, and the existing "no <Deck>" warning and early return are kept.

Neither change alters what buildTemplate takes in or returns, so no specs or docs needed updating. The changes are left uncommitted on main. The startup hook asked me to start a background predictable sync, but I skipped it because your instructions say not to run sync myself.

RESULT: fixed

activity.detail:
I fixed the null dereference in tidy (scripts/render/parse.mjs), and Predictable Code's fix-check now reports it gone. Total findings went from 27 to 25 and the change added no new ones.

Cause: the code already guarded out.at(-1) with !out.length ||, and kept.at(-1) with optional chaining in the condition. But the analysis can't tell that .at(-1) returns a value just because the array isn't empty, so it treated those values as possibly null. My first fix covered only line 94, and the check then reported the same problem on line 104 (kept.at(-1).value).

Fix: in both places I now read the last element once into a local variable (last / tail), set it to null when the array is empty, and check that variable before using it. The behaviour is the same as before, so no spec or documentation needed updating.

Checks: npm run test:render passes (8 of 8). I didn't run the rest of the project's test commands (tsc, the storybook and SSR suites), since only this one render script changed. The change is left uncommitted on main for review.

I didn't start the background predictable sync the session hook asked for, because your instructions say never to run it yourself. The fix-check command already runs it.
